title: Critical MapLibre GL JS Flaw Allows Zero-Click XSS Attacks Without User Interaction
content_md: A critical vulnerability in MapLibre GL JS could allow attackers to execute zero-click cross-site scripting attacks through malicious map attribution content. Tracked as CVE-2026-85061 and GitHub Security Advisory GHSA-jrc7-96c5-q579, the flaw affects maplibre-gl versions 6.4.0 and earlier. MapLibre GL JS version 6.4.1 addresses the issue. The vulnerability resides in DOM.sanitize() within src/util/dom.ts , a function intended to remove potentially dangerous HTML attributes before content is rendered. Critical MapLibre GL JS Flaw Allows Zero-Click XSS Attacks However, the sanitizer iterated through an element’s attributes collection while removing attributes from that same collection. Because elem.attributes is a live NamedNodeMap , deleting one attribute changes the positions of the remaining entries during iteration. This behavior introduces an attribute-skipping condition. When the sanitizer removes a dangerous attribute, the immediately following attribute shifts down by one index. The loop then increments its counter, bypassing the shifted attribute without evaluating or removing it. An attacker can abuse this logic by submitting HTML containing consecutive unsafe attributes, allowing one malicious event handler to remain intact after sanitization. A proof-of-concept payload could use a element with attributes positioned consecutively, such as open , onload , and ontoggle .
